worksheet.title: Fix the Mix-Up
worksheet.subtitle: Find the mistake and fix it
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the one card that is wrong and fix it.

parts.title: Bit made a mistake
parts.text: Bit was making a pattern, but one card is wrong. Finding and fixing a mistake is called DEBUGGING. Circle the wrong card, then say what it should be.

parts.title: Watch Bit — this should go ● ▲ ● ▲ …
parts.note: The 5th card is a square ■, but the pattern needs a circle ●. That square is the mix-up.

parts.title: Fix the group
parts.prompt: These should all be circles. Circle the one that does not belong, and say what it should be.

parts.title: Fix the pattern
parts.prompt: This should go ★ ■ ★ ■ … . Circle the card that is wrong, and say what it should be.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: This should go ▲ ● ▲ ● … . Circle the card that is wrong, and say what it should be.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Finding a mistake and fixing it is called debugging. Every coder debugs — even the best ones make mix-ups and then fix them!

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children find the one card that breaks a pattern or group and say what it should be. Spotting and fixing a mistake is a first thinking-skill behind coding — the K-friendly first taste of debugging. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud; the child circles the wrong card and names the fix out loud. Optional: build a pattern with blocks, slip in a wrong one, and have children find it.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Read circle, triangle, circle, triangle, square, triangle aloud: "it should be circle–triangle… but here is a square — that is the mix-up." Circle it; it should be a circle.
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — the triangle does not belong in the circle group.
3. Let them try. Children fix Exercise 2 and Exercise 3 on their own.

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — circle, circle, triangle, circle → circle the triangle; it should be a circle.

Exercise 2 — star, square, star, square, star, star → circle the last card; it should be a square. Exercise 3 — triangle, circle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle → circle the last card; it should be a circle.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: circling more than one. There is exactly one mix-up; have them read to the end first.
Make it easier: use a short 4-card pattern with the mistake near the start.
Make it harder: have the child make a pattern with a mix-up for a partner to find and fix.
Make it active: clap a pattern, slip in a wrong clap, and have children call out the mix-up.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children detect and correct an error in a sequence or group.
In plain terms: finding the one thing that is wrong and saying how to fix it — a first taste of debugging.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by drawing or circling.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child circles the single wrong card in each item and names the correct shape it should be.
